newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Conditions in Ramallah bleak after 5-day siege.
newsitem.headline: Conditions in Ramallah bleak after 5-day siege.

text.p: Palestinian cabinet minister Hanan Ashrawi said on Monday a five-day-old Israeli siege of Ramallah has severely disrupted health and educational services in the West Bank city.
Ashrawi, minister of higher education, said Ramallah's main hospital had suspended normal surgical operations and was dealing only with emergencies.

"Hospitals say right now they have supplies but they're running low on fresh produce, I don't know how long Ramallah can last in this state of siege," she said in an address to the Foreign Press Association.

Israel imposed a closure on Ramallah, cutting it off from other parts of the West Bank, on Wednesday following the killing near the city of two Jewish settlers by gunmen belonging to the Damascus-based Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

Ashrawi said the Palestinian Authority, which demanded the lifting of the siege, "only had hints from Israel that this will not last long but we judge on the basis of actions and not hints and public relations""
A parliamentary official quoted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as saying on Monday the blockade could be lifted soon.

"The closure on Ramallah will not last for very long -- among other reasons, because some of the suspects have been arrested," Netanyahu told parliament's foreign affairs and defence committee, referring to Wednesday's attack.
Ashrawi said shops were closed in Ramallah since storeowners from surrounding areas could not enter the city.

"Schools as well have been entirely disrupted because teachers can't come from nearby villages. This morning Ramallah hospital sent an SOS because not only are the doctors unable to come to Ramallah but patients as well aren't able to enter," she said.
The Ramallah blockade marked the third time Israel has imposed so-called internal closures in the West Bank.
Israel imposed an overall closure of the West Bank and Gaza Strip after suicide bombings by Moslem militants killed 59 people in the Jewish state last February and March.
The closure has been eased intermittently, allowing less than 40,000 Palestinians working in Israel to return to their jobs.
The PLO has described the closure as "collective punishment" and said it wass destroying an already weak Palestinian economy.

Ashrawi said conditions in the West Bank and Gaza Strip were very tense and Palestinian frustration was mounting as a result of "the continued closure, the on-going land confiscation by Israel, expansion and building of Jewish settlements on Palestinian land, and not implementing signed agreements."
"Netanyahu himself is guilty of provocation, of incitement, of preparing all the conditions for confrontations, conflict and violence," she said.
